exercise.name: Kettlebell Swing

reference.title: Kettlebell Swing
reference.listing: Video (movement reference; page text could not be fetched at authoring time, title from the link)
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

exercise.mechanics: Compound (explosive hip extension from a hinge; arms swing passively)

breathing.pattern: Breathe in as the bell falls into the hinge, short sharp breath out as the hips snap.

prescription.load: User-chosen kettlebell; stop the set when the hips slow or the back starts to round
prescription.progression: Heavier kettlebell, longer sets, then one-arm swings

cues.text: Feet a little wider than the hips, toes slightly out, kettlebell handle in both hands, palms toward you.
Hinge: push the hips back and hike the bell high between the thighs, forearms close to them.
Snap the hips forward and stand tall; the bell floats to chest height on straight arms.
Let it fall; hinge late and hike it back between the legs.
Snap again: glutes tight, ribs down, no leaning back.
Let the bell slow and stop hanging in front.

mistakes.fix: Hinge: hips go back, shins stay nearly vertical.
Let the hip snap float the bell; the arms are ropes.
Finish tall in a straight line with the glutes squeezed.

mistakes.mistake: Letting the bell drop low toward the knees
mistakes.fix: Hike it high between the thighs, close to the groin.

mistakes.mistake: Rounding the back at the bottom
mistakes.fix: Keep the chest proud and the back flat through the hinge.

kinematics.setup: ≈90° at the bottom (joint channel), trunk ≈45° forward
kinematics.norm: Kettlebell swing: about 75 degrees of hip flexion at the start to about 1 degree of extension at the top (McGill 2012)
About 69 degrees at the bottom to about 2 degrees of extension at the top in the kettlebell swing (McGill 2012); a hinge, not a squat

kinematics.setup: Arms 20° behind vertical, kettlebell between the thighs
kinematics.peak: Arms ≈84° forward at the top: hands at about 128 cm, shoulders 133 cm
kinematics.norm: Kettlebell floats to about chest height (Russian swing; clinical opinion)

kinematics.setup: Hands side by side on the handle, grip points 7.5 cm apart
kinematics.norm: Both hands on the handle, overhand (clinical opinion)

kinematics.peak: About 1.5 s per swing (0.7 s up, 0.8 s down), two swings, then park
kinematics.norm: Fast contraction-relaxation cycles over about half a second (McGill 2012); about 1.5 s per swing (clinical opinion)

sources.title: McGill & Marshall 2012, kettlebell swing, snatch, and bottoms-up carry: back and hip muscle activation, motion, and low back loads (J Strength Cond Res 26(1):16-27)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, numbness, tingling or giving-way occurs.
The kettlebell load is your choice: pick a weight you can move with the form shown for every rep.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Fast lift: learn the hinge slowly with a light kettlebell first and clear a space in front of and behind you.
Low-back pain: peak swing compression was about 3.2 kN in McGill 2012; build up slowly and stop if pain increases.
modify: Tight hamstrings: bend the knees a little more, keep the back flat.

muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Snap the hips forward: about 76% MVC in the gluteus maximus during kettlebell swings (McGill 2012).
muscleNotes.glute_max_l: Snap the hips forward: about 76% MVC in the gluteus maximus during kettlebell swings (McGill 2012).
muscleNotes.hamstrings_r: Load in the hinge and drive the hip extension.
muscleNotes.hamstrings_l: Load in the hinge and drive the hip extension.
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_r: Hold the flat back against the swing: about 45% MVC in the lumbar erectors (McGill 2012).
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_l: Hold the flat back against the swing: about 45% MVC in the lumbar erectors (McGill 2012).
muscleNotes.glute_med_r: Active with the glutes in the snap (about 70% MVC, McGill 2012).
muscleNotes.glute_med_l: Active with the glutes in the snap (about 70% MVC, McGill 2012).
muscleNotes.quads_r: Straighten the soft knees at the top.
muscleNotes.quads_l: Straighten the soft knees at the top.
muscleNotes.adductors_r: Help extend the hips from the wide stance.
muscleNotes.adductors_l: Help extend the hips from the wide stance.
muscleNotes.core: Brace at the top so the swing ends in a straight line, not a back bend.
muscleNotes.obliques_r: Brace with the abdominals at the top of the swing (McGill 2012).
muscleNotes.obliques_l: Brace with the abdominals at the top of the swing (McGill 2012).
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_r: Guides the bell to chest height; the arms do not lift it.
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_l: Guides the bell to chest height; the arms do not lift it.
muscleNotes.lats_r: Keep the arms close to the body on the way down (hike the bell back).
muscleNotes.lats_l: Keep the arms close to the body on the way down (hike the bell back).
